text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian papers this morning:

-One in four Norwegians believe that Norwegian cross-country skiers take some form of performance-enhancing drug, an opinion poll shows. Jan Jansen, president of the Norwegian Ski Federation, says the sport has a credibility problem and that it is unjust.

-Kripos, the central police division for serious crime, will not help Tromsoe police in the investigation into a fire at a refugee centre because of cost cuts. Tromsoe police say there are several suspicious circumstances behind the fire and they need expert help. Two people were treated for shock in blaze, which completely destroyed the building.
-Stockbrokers earned too much and investors pay too much for their services, says fund manager Petter Goldenheim at Odin Forvaltning.
-Norwegian truck transport companies have severe financial problems. One third of the companies have negative equity capital.

-Norwegian shipyards have taken losses because of recent developments in the foreign exchange markets. All of the largest foreign competitors have experienced a more favorable exchange rate against the dollar.
